stem: Obtain the binding energy (in MeV) of a nitrogen nucleus \(\left({}^{14}_{7}\text{N}\right)\), given \(m\left({}^{14}_{7}\text{N}\right) = 14.00307\,\text{u}\).
_note: The EXERCISES block opens with a shared data table that the printed questions rely on rather than restate: \(1\,\text{u} = 931.5\,\text{MeV}/c^2\), \(m_{\text{H}} = 1.007825\,\text{u}\), \(m_{\text{n}} = 1.008665\,\text{u}\), \(m({}^{4}_{2}\text{He}) = 4.002603\,\text{u}\), \(m_{\text{e}} = 0.000548\,\text{u}\), \(1\,\text{MeV} = 1.6\times10^{-13}\,\text{J}\), \(N = 6.023\times10^{23}\) per mole, \(1\,\text{year} = 3.154\times10^{7}\,\text{s}\). Stems are transcribed as printed; these constants are not repeated into each stem.

stem:
Obtain the binding energy of the nuclei \({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\) and \({}^{209}_{83}\text{Bi}\) in units of MeV from the following data:

\(m({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}) = 55.934939\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{209}_{83}\text{Bi}) = 208.980388\,\text{u}\)

A given coin has a mass of \(3.0\,\text{g}\). Calculate the nuclear energy that would be required to separate all the neutrons and protons from each other. For simplicity assume that the coin is entirely made of \({}^{63}_{29}\text{Cu}\) atoms (of mass \(62.92960\,\text{u}\)).
Obtain approximately the ratio of the nuclear radii of the gold isotope \({}^{197}_{79}\text{Au}\) and the silver isotope \({}^{107}_{47}\text{Ag}\).

The \(Q\) value of a nuclear reaction \(A + b \to C + d\) is defined by

\(Q = [\,m_A + m_b - m_C - m_d\,]c^2\)

where the masses refer to the respective nuclei. Determine from the given data the \(Q\)-value of the following reaction and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

(i) \({}^{1}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{3}_{1}\text{H} \to {}^{2}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{2}_{1}\text{H}\)

Atomic masses are given to be

\(m({}^{2}_{1}\text{H}) = 2.014102\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{3}_{1}\text{H}) = 3.016049\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{12}_{6}\text{C}) = 12.000000\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{20}_{10}\text{Ne}) = 19.992439\,\text{u}\)

The \(Q\) value of a nuclear reaction \(A + b \to C + d\) is defined by

\(Q = [\,m_A + m_b - m_C - m_d\,]c^2\)

where the masses refer to the respective nuclei. Determine from the given data the \(Q\)-value of the following reaction and state whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic.

(ii) \({}^{12}_{6}\text{C} + {}^{12}_{6}\text{C} \to {}^{20}_{10}\text{Ne} + {}^{4}_{2}\text{He}\)

Atomic masses are given to be

\(m({}^{2}_{1}\text{H}) = 2.014102\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{3}_{1}\text{H}) = 3.016049\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{12}_{6}\text{C}) = 12.000000\,\text{u}\)

\(m({}^{20}_{10}\text{Ne}) = 19.992439\,\text{u}\)

Suppose, we think of fission of a \({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}\) nucleus into two equal fragments, \({}^{28}_{13}\text{Al}\). Is the fission energetically possible? Argue by working out \(Q\) of the process. Given \(m({}^{56}_{26}\text{Fe}) = 55.93494\,\text{u}\) and \(m({}^{28}_{13}\text{Al}) = 27.98191\,\text{u}\).

The fission properties of \({}^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}\) are very similar to those of \({}^{235}_{92}\text{U}\). The average energy released per fission is \(180\,\text{MeV}\). How much energy, in MeV, is released if all the atoms in \(1\,\text{kg}\) of pure \({}^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}\) undergo fission?

How long can an electric lamp of \(100\,\text{W}\) be kept glowing by fusion of \(2.0\,\text{kg}\) of deuterium? Take the fusion reaction as

\({}^{2}_{1}\text{H} + {}^{2}_{1}\text{H} \to {}^{3}_{2}\text{He} + \text{n} + 3.27\,\text{MeV}\)

Calculate the height of the potential barrier for a head on collision of two deuterons. (Hint: The height of the potential barrier is given by the Coulomb repulsion between the two deuterons when they just touch each other. Assume that they can be taken as hard spheres of radius \(2.0\,\text{fm}\).)
From the relation \(R = R_0 A^{1/3}\), where \(R_0\) is a constant and \(A\) is the mass number of a nucleus, show that the nuclear matter density is nearly constant (i.e. independent of \(A\)).
